questions.questionText:
The diameter of a copper wire is thought to be approximately 0.3mm.
Which instrument should be used to obtain a more accurate measurement of the diameter of the
wire?

An object is released from rest and falls to Earth. During its fall, the object is affected by air
resistance. The air resistance eventually reaches a constant value.
Which description about successive stages of the motion of the object is correct?

A concrete post is carried up a very high mountain. At the top of the mountain, the gravitational
field is slightly weaker than at the bottom.
What is the effect of this weaker field on the mass and on the weight of the post at the top of the
mountain?
mass weight
Which is the value of a vector quantity?

The table gives four energy sources and states whether the energy of the source is derived from
the Sun.
Which row is correct?
source of energy derived from the Sun

questions.questionText:
A force acts on an area to produce a pressure.
Which changes produce the same pressure?

options.text: double the area and double the force
double the area and halve the force
double the area and make the force four times bigger
halve the area and double the force

questions.questionText:
Gases can be compressed, but liquids cannot.
Which statement explains this difference?

options.text: Each molecule in a gas is more compressible than each molecule in a liquid.
Molecules in a gas are further apart than molecules in a liquid.
Molecules in a gas attract each other more strongly than molecules in a liquid.
Molecules in a gas move more slowly than molecules in a liquid.

questions.questionText: Which quantity gives the thermal capacity of a solid object?

options.text: the energy lost by radiation from the object in 1.0s
the energy needed to melt the object
the energy needed to raise the temperature of the object by 1.0°C
the total amount of thermal energy in the object

questions.questionText:
To mark a temperature scale on a thermometer, standard temperatures known as fixed points are
needed.
Which of these is a fixed point on the Celsius scale?

options.text: the temperature of pure melting ice
the temperature of pure warm water

questions.questionText:
In an experiment, a liquid is heated at a constant rate.
The temperature of the liquid increases and eventually becomes constant.
Which statement about the experiment is correct?

options.text: Boiling occurs at all temperatures but only on the liquid surface.
Boiling occurs throughout the liquid but only at the constant temperature.
Evaporation occurs throughout the liquid and at all temperatures.
Evaporation occurs only at the constant temperature and only on the liquid surface.

questions.questionText:
One end of a copper rod is heated.
What is one method by which thermal energy is transferred in the copper rod?

options.text: Free electrons transfer energy from the cooler end to the hotter end.
Free electrons transfer energy from the hotter end to the cooler end.
Molecules of copper move from the cooler end to the hotter end.
Molecules of copper move from the hotter end to the cooler end.

questions.questionText:
Two plastic cups are placed one inside the other. A small spacer keeps the two cups separated.
Hot water is poured into the inner cup and a lid is put on top, as shown.
lid
small spacer
small air gap
hot water
bench
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The bench is heated by convection from the bottom of the outer cup.
The lid reduces the energy lost by convection.
There is no thermal conduction through the sides of either cup.
Thermal radiation is prevented by the small air gap.

method 1: place it in an east-west direction and hammer it

method 4: put it slowly into a coil that is carrying a direct current

A battery charger plugs into a 230V a.c. supply. The charger is used to charge a 6.0V d.c.
battery.
The charger contains diodes and a transformer.
What is the purpose of these components?
diodes transformer

options.text: rectify the a.c. steps down the voltage
rectify the a.c. steps up the voltage
step down the voltage rectifies the a.c.
step up the voltage rectifies the a.c.

reading on reading on

What is the greatest hazard?

magnetic field

questions.questionText:
The scattering of α-particles by a thin metal foil supports the nuclear model of an atom.
Why are α-particles used rather than neutrons?

options.text: because they always travel more slowly
because they are larger in diameter
because they have a positive charge

questions.questionText:
A nucleus of a radioactive substance 218Po undergoes an α-decay followed by a β-decay.
What are the nucleon (mass) number and proton (atomic) number of the nuclide formed after
both decays have happened?
nucleon number proton number

A scientist carries out an experiment using a sealed source which emits β-particles. The range of
the β-particles in the air is about 30cm.
Which precaution is the most effective to protect the scientist from the radiation?

options.text: handling the source with long tongs
keeping the temperature of the source low
opening all windows in the laboratory
washing his hands before leaving the laboratory
